Who is Voltiris? Voltiris is a Dutch-Swiss startup that has developed the world's first solar energy system that fully integrates in greenhouses. Light frequencies required for crop growth are passed on the plants, the rest is turned into large-scale renewable energy. This way we turn greenhouses into net energy producers. Voltiris is a fast growing startup team of 40 people across our Swiss and Dutch offices. We have projects live in greenhouses in The Netherlands, Belgium, France and Switzerland. To support this acceleration, we are looking for Business Analysts. What does the internship involve? As Business Analyst intern you join the Commercial Operations team in The Hague. You'll do the analysis behind every customer conversation. In practice you will: - Build pre-feasibility studies for growers, using their energy consumption, tariffs, greenhouse characteristics and site constraints - Model the business case: energy savings, production impact, payback and ROI - Prepare the numbers behind proposals and presentations for our Sales Managers, including our North America lead - Check customer data, spot gaps and inconsistencies, and go back to the source when something doesn't add up - Improve and standardise the models and templates the commercial team uses - Contribute to market analysis that shapes where we focus next Practical details: 6 months, full-time with at least 60% in our The Hague office. Starting date is flexible. We're looking for someone who could consider staying full-time after the internship. What are we looking for? - A degree in Engineering, Energy, Economics, Business, Agriculture or another quantitative field - Strong in Excel is a plus - Familiarity with AI tools - Curious and critical: you don't accept a result you can't explain - You like supporting a team and working to their deadlines - You're comfortable in a startup where processes are still being built - Fluent English; Dutch, German or French ...

Fellowship in Paintings Conservation SRAL is offering a fellowship (full-time, 40h) in the Paintings Conservation Department. The one-year fellowship will commence on May 1st, 2027 and include a monthly stipend of €2850,- gross. SRAL Fellowship in Paintings Conservation Working under the guidance of the SRAL conservators the fellow will focus on practical conservation and restoration treatments as well as on a research project. The fellow will work as part of the team and participate in the daily activities of the conservation studio, focusing on easel paintings on canvas and possibly panel. Also, they may have the opportunity to join conservation work on site. The intern will carry out a range of conservation treatments including technical examination, photographic as well as written documentation. They also will be encouraged to participate in the decision-making processes. Participation in workshops, lectures and occasional studio visits will contribute to the fellowship programme. Although the research project's initial outline will be provided by SRAL conservators, its ultimate direction and scope will be decided in close consultation with the fellow. Eligibility Applicants hold a master's degree in conservation. They should have a maximum of two years of professional experience post-graduation. Alongside proficiency in English a demonstrated aptitude for research and writing is an advantage. The position is open to candidates of all nationalities. Candidates are responsible for securing visas and other permits for their stay and work in the Netherlands. (SRAL is not a registered sponsor at IND).
